## The idea

Two performances can use the same pitches and nominal durations while sounding
unrelated. One clips every note at half its slot. Another lets notes overlap,
leans on the high point, and nudges an arrival late. The score states events;
performance shapes their realisation.

*Articulation* controls how notes connect. Dynamics control amplitude over time.
Phrasing groups events into gestures through accents, timing, and contour. I
found it useful to preserve a strict event layer and pass it to two renderers.
Then expressive choices remain inspectable instead of leaking into the score.

## Run this

```{.ruby audio=""}
use_bpm 82
use_synth :piano

score = [
  {note: :c4, start: 0, duration: 1},
  {note: :d4, start: 1, duration: 1},
  {note: :e4, start: 2, duration: 1},
  {note: :g4, start: 3, duration: 2},
  {note: :e4, start: 5, duration: 1},
  {note: :d4, start: 6, duration: 1},
  {note: :c4, start: 7, duration: 2}
]

define :play_events do |events, shaped|
  cursor = 0
  events.each_with_index do |event, index|
    sleep event[:start] - cursor
    high_point = event[:note] == :g4
    amp = shaped ? (0.55 + index * 0.05 + (high_point ? 0.2 : 0)) : 0.7
    ratio = shaped ? (high_point ? 1.05 : 0.82) : 0.5
    offset = shaped && index == 4 ? 0.08 : 0
    sleep offset
    play event[:note], sustain: event[:duration] * ratio,
      release: 0.08, amp: amp
    sleep event[:duration] - offset
    cursor = event[:start] + event[:duration]
  end
end

play_events score, false
sleep 2
play_events score, true
```

The strict renderer gives every event equal amplitude and detached length. The
shaped renderer grows toward G, sustains the high point, and delays the following
E by a small amount. Pitch and nominal event boundaries remain in one shared
score.

## Change one thing

1. Set the strict ratio to `1.05`. The notes overlap and the strict version turns
   legato without changing any event.
2. Move the accent from G to the final C. The phrase now reserves its strongest
   amplitude for arrival instead of climax.
3. Increase the onset offset from `0.08` to `0.3`. The expressive hesitation
   becomes a timing error and compresses the remaining duration.

## Why it works

Each event follows the shared schema: `:note`, `:start`, and `:duration`. Start
is an onset on the score timeline, while duration reserves a slot. The renderer
chooses how much of that slot sounds and at what amplitude. This distinction
prevents staccato from corrupting metric totals.

Expression becomes a function from structural events to playback parameters.
The high-point test derives emphasis from pitch. The crescendo derives it from
index. The offset targets one event. These policies can be replaced without
editing source notes.

A perfectly quantised version may sound rigid, but the amount and direction of
useful deviation depend on style. The code offers an audible comparison to
assess in Sonic Pi. Syntax validation cannot establish that the shaped pass is
better or that the offset is perceptible on a given system.

Amplitude is also perceived relative to its neighbours. Setting every event to
`0.9` makes the phrase louder without creating a high point. A crescendo creates
direction because successive values form a slope. An accent creates a local
contrast. These are different policies even when they produce the same amplitude
on one note.

The renderer currently sleeps through each event, so a positive onset offset
reduces the available sounding slot. Another design could preserve duration and
push all later starts, changing the whole timeline. Neither interpretation is
hidden once score time and performance time have separate variables. Choose the
policy that matches the musical instruction and state it in the renderer name
or its input fields.

## Take it further

Add `:amp` and `:articulation` fields to selected score events. Support
`:staccato`, `:legato`, and `:accent` in `play_events`, using renderer defaults
when a field is absent. Produce three performances from the same score: detached,
fully legato, and phrase-shaped. No pitch, start, or duration value may change.
